text:
ops-incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: US-WEST runtime p95 latency spike + throughput drop observed. Auto-mitigation triggered: canary traffic cut to 10%. Paging oncall.
devon: on it, jumping in. seeing kernel fallback traces in logs - a lot of `kernel_selector` fallbacks to slow path.
sara: confirming, dashboards show batch window increase and queue length up. Canary deployment `release/2026-03-17/rv2` rolled at ~1766598000.
anya: any customer errors? sales-ops, do you have live reports?
sales-ops: customers A & D reported slow responses on chat flows, 2 support tickets open. No 5xx rate increase yet. Impact seems latency-only right now.
mike: reproducing locally — when kernel fallback happens, batching accumulates but processing is much slower -> throughput drops. Likely a kernel selection heuristic mismatch for new microbatch config.
devon: this matches the canary change: we shipped `adaptive_microbatch=true` + new kernel hints. Can flip the feature flag.
sara: agree we need to kill the flag, then either rollback or full revert. Recommendation: flip kill-switch for canary first to stop further degradation, then decide on rollback.
ops-incident-bot: ACTION LOG: oncall devon acknowledged at 1766601150.
devon: executing: `ffctl set adaptive_microbatch=false --scope=canary --id=rl-20260317-42`
mike: got it, kernels stop falling back after flag flip on canary nodes. p95 trending down but slow tail remains.
anya: can you route all canary traffic to stable while we validate? We should avoid user-facing rollback if flag flip stabilizes.
devon: routing: `redwood route update --cluster=us-west --from=release/2026-03-17/rv2 --to=stable --percent=0` (will cut canary traffic). Doing a gradual shift now.
sara: monitoring: latency p95 back to baseline within 3 minutes on most pods, some hosts still showing slow KV eviction.
mike: eviction logs show throttled IO on 3 GPU hosts, possibly unrelated noisy neighbor. I'm triggering a pod restart on those hosts to clear KV state.
sales-ops: telling affected customers we're investigating and applying mitigation, no SLA hits expected at this time.
anya: if restarts don't clear persistent slow kernels, prepare for full rollback `redwood rollout revert rl-20260317-42` — flag change is lower-risk though.
devon: restarts done, p95 stable. I'll keep canary traffic at 0% and watch for 15m before re-enabling.
ops-incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (flag kill-switch + canary traffic cut). Severity downgraded to P2.
sara: handing off to eng-oncall for post-deploy follow-up and postmortem. devon/anya/two-hour follow-up window to validate no regression.
mike: note for postmortem: look at kernel selector thresholds and microbatch heuristic interplay + pod IO saturation correlation.
devon: thanks team. If anything spikes again ping me and I'll initiate rollback.
sales-ops: I'll draft a short customer note summarizing action.
anya: tagging for postmortem: @mike @devon @sara.
sara: closing paging channel in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
